what: Leads the precedent chain in the handoff has already decided. They stay in the queue and are recorded as drops with the precedent as the reason, never deleted. No research is owed on them. The certifier entry carries a CONFIRM step: read the respondent's stated role before recording it.

drops.reason: An event rights-holder, licensor, franchisor, promoter or sanctioning body fails test 1 and sits below a buyer. Round 46 cut the Bahrain Grand Prix case on this: a local promoter pays a fee for the right to stage the event, so the money leaves the host country rather than entering it, and the rights-holder puts in no capital, holds no stake, insures nothing and sets no condition. The UK NCP assessment says at paragraph 26 that the information does not link the companies to any abuses, and at 28 that promoting a high-profile event which attracts protests does not itself link them.

A paid auditor, certifier, consultant, ratings agency or law firm fails test 1. Round 46 cut the Rana Plaza case on this: a certifier monetises a representation about risk and carries none of the loss, which is the element that makes an insurer a funding tie. It fails even where reliance on the certificate was real. CONFIRM before recording: check that this respondent acted only as a certifier here, and held no stake and set no condition.
